descriptionChirho: A copper-based metal (bronze or copper) used for implements, fetters, and structural elements in ancient Israel. All occurrences refer to the same base metal regardless of prepositional framing (bare noun, simile 'like bronze'). Cross-lingual evidence is unanimous: Arabic نُحَاسٌ/نُحَاسٍ (nuhas), Swahili 'shaba' (copper/brass), Hindi पीतल (pital, brass) and काँसा (kaansa, bronze), Korean 동 (dong, copper), Spanish 'bronce.' The ancient Hebrew term did not distinguish copper from bronze alloy, as confirmed by the interchangeability of 'bronze' and 'copper' renderings across all target languages.
